intent: Kept the 16 mm footprint at x = ±0.05 m, five sensors, wheels, body and the 0.12 m track from the best-scoring iteration 2 row. Changed mass back to 0.8 kg, since 0.6 kg gave no gain, and changed sensor y from 0.04 to 0.02 m as the single exploratory test. I expect max_error to fall to about 0.058 m or below with line loss at zero, giving a score at or above 26.99. I am considering, without committing, a y of 0.00 m if 0.02 m reduces max_error with no line loss. I am not considering body or footprint changes, because the off-track floor cannot rise above 0.06 m and footprint has shown no effect.
learning: Iterations 1 to 5 show span removes line loss, while footprint, wheel track, mass and look-ahead (y 0.06) do not reduce the 0.061 m excursion. Shifting the row to y = 0.02 tests whether the excursion is an entry transient tied to look-ahead. Ask the Integrator to report whether the excursion occurs at the start of the run or at a specific bend, and whether line loss is affected by the shorter look-ahead.
rationale: Iterations 0 to 5 all ended off_track with max_error of about 0.061 m. Span ±0.05 m removed line loss (iteration 1), and footprint (16 mm), wheel_track (0.15 m) and mass (0.6 kg) left max_error unchanged. Iteration 5 (0.6 kg) scored 26.9876 against 26.9949 at 0.8 kg, and its max_error was 0.0617, 0.0605 and 0.0616 on oval, s-bend and slalom, so yaw inertia is not the excursion. Look-ahead y = 0.06 did not move max_error and brought line loss back. The Integrator's contingency now applies: line loss is zero and max_error stays near 0.061 m, so I propose one start-up geometry change. I am taking the Integrator's advice in part. I revert mass to 0.8 kg because the 0.6 kg gain was not measurable and 0.8 kg is the best-scoring row. I move sensor y from 0.04 to 0.02 m, a shorter look-ahead, which the Integrator named as untested. The hypothesis is that the excursion is a start-up or entry transient driven by the sensor row reading the line too far ahead of the axle, so a row nearer the axle should reduce the early overshoot. The lead-lag evidence is consistent with this: y = 0.06 added line loss, so a shorter look-ahead should reduce it. I expect line_loss_events to stay at zero and max_error to fall to or below about 0.058 m. If line loss returns, the shorter look-ahead is not usable, and I will revert to y = 0.04.
